newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia tries to meet German firms over gas sale.
newsitem.headline: Latvia tries to meet German firms over gas sale.

text.p: Latvia will remove some of the obstacles preventing a final deal on the sale of a stake in its gas company to German Ruhrgas and Preussen but cannot meet all the Western firms' requests, officials said on Wednesday.
Ruhrgas and Preussen joined to share around a 30 percent stake in Latvian Gas with Russia's Gazprom.
The German firms want the Latvian government to secure the company's debts, expected to be some 34 million lats this year.
"The Germans are ready to take the risk of future activity but do not want to be responsible for debts," Viktor Shadinov, privatisation agency legal director, told a news conference.
"Certain sums have been found by the prime minister but they are not as big as the Germans would like," he added.
The final sale agreement with the German firms has been postponed twice and Latvia hoped to sign it next month.
The privatisation agency is expecting to receive a reaction on Latvia's proposals from the German side later on Wednesday.
Latvian Gas is one of the state energy monopolies on offer along with electricity supply firm Latvenergo.
